title: Postmortem prospectus and staging sim notes - May 2026 (draft)
summary: Working prospectus for how we'll shape postmortem-friendly signal capture during the May rollout. The idea is to run a focused staging sim that exercises the tiered fallback and produces structured artifacts so the eventual postmortem is evidence-first and decisions are traceable.
objectives: Validate fallback chain under region-local surge (multi-region sim)
Exercise KV-cache warmup and cold-start telemetry under sustained bursts
Produce standardized signal bundles (traffic, latency, error, model-variant) for postmortem ingestion
Document decision threads (who flips which switch and when) to shorten RCA time
timeline: Week of May 10: prep and run sims. Day 0 (May 11): dry run with synthetic traffic; Day 1 (May 12): staged canary with 10% traffic; Day 2 (May 13): escalate to 30% then trigger controlled throttle to test rollback. Reserve May 14 for artifact collection and quick sync.
staging-sim-checklist: Provision sim cluster: 4 small GPU nodes + 2 control plane replicas
Load generator: configure sequence distribution to match prod QPS P95 (see linked Confluence artifact)
Seed KV-cache prefixes for the top 50 prompts to avoid over-counting cold starts
Enable full tracing (sample rate 100%) for sim window; disable retention to 90 days only for these runs
Attach a dedicated storage bucket for signal bundles: s3://redwood-release-sims/may-2026/<run-id>
Annotate every manual action in the sim timeline (Slack thread and runbook task list)
Smoke test rollback path — test canary abort, model-variant fallback, and region re-route
decision-threads: We need a clear mapping of decision authority during the sim and the real rollout. Propose: Release Lead (Leah) owns go/no-go; SRE (Ravi) owns throttle and routing toggles; Model Ops (Sophie) owns variant pin/rollforward. Every decision must log the Jira key, time, and rationale in the Slack thread and the run artifact bundle.
telemetry-anchors: cost.token_burn_rate — track delta vs baseline during ramp
rollback-matrix: Soft rollback: reduce canary to previous stable model variant and enable burst-throttle (operator action). Hard rollback: shift region routing to fallback region and drain new instances; if error_rate stays > 1% for 15m after soft rollback, escalate to hard rollback. Record timestamps and who executed each step.
open-questions: Do we want 100% trace sampling for the production-like sim? cost vs signal tradeoff needs sign-off (Ravi)
Should model variant tagging include a short- lived 'sim' tag to avoid confusion in catalog? (Sophie)
Retention window for sim traces — default 90 days or extend to 180 for deeper RCA?
Who owns the final postmortem write-up and SLA impact calc? (ops vs product)
notes: Notes to self: keep the sim tight (2-3 hours max) to avoid churn. Bring an observer from customer-success for any sim that touches Dedicated customers. Link back the artifact bundle to REL-3421 and file a short postmortem skeleton within 48h. Expect some friction around KV-cache seeding; allocate 2 hours pre-run for that. Quick commands: infra/provision-sim.sh --region us-west2 --nodes 4; loadgen/run --profile prod-like --duration 60m.
post-sim-actions: Collect signal bundle and run extractor: tools/signal-extract --src s3://redwood-release-sims/may-2026/<run-id> --out /tmp/signals.tgz
Populate REL-3421 with initial timeline and attach signals.tgz
Schedule 1h post-sim sync within 4 hours of run completion
Draft postmortem skeleton (owner Leah) and request comments from collaborators within 72h
